data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (multiple images show leaflets arranged in distinct pairs along the rachis, with the terminal leaflet positioned at the end)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaflets are spaced along the rachis rather than clustered at the tip)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (leaflets are distinct and attached to a central axis, the rachis)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (each leaf has a single terminal leaflet at the apex of the rachis)
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 7 (the most complete leaf visible in the images has three pairs of leaflets plus a terminal leaflet)
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): opposite (leaflets are arranged in pairs at nodes along the rachis)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (the leaf margins appear smooth, though some leaves have holes from damage)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaflets are broadly oval with the widest part near the middle)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (the tips of the leaflets come to a distinct point)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (the base of the leaflets appears generally rounded to slightly obtuse)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with secondary veins branching off it)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible and prominent, arranged in a pinnate pattern, appearing to number around 8-10 pairs
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (the leaflets reflect light, indicating a smooth, somewhat glossy surface)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs are visible on the leaf surface)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): long (the rachis and petiole are significantly longer than the individual leaflets)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the petiole and rachis appear round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stem appears green, slender, and non-woody)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stem surface appears smooth without visible hairs)
    19.	Stem color: green (the main stem and rachis are green)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface appears smooth)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are clearly visible at the leaf nodes)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen pulvinus is visible at the base of the leaflets or petiole)
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: Some leaflets exhibit damage, including holes and missing margin sections. A pink ribbon is tied to the stem.
